record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Does there exist an irrational polygon, meaning a polygon whose angles are not all rational multiples of π, that is nonergodic as a billiard table?

evidence.quote: Задача 8. Привести пример иррационального неэргодического многоугольника.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A billiard in a planar polygon $P$ is the dynamical system describing the free motion of a point particle inside $P$ that reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary, with vertices treated as singular. The billiard flow preserves Liouville measure (Lebesgue measure on the unit tangent bundle of $P$, restricted to inward-pointing vectors at the boundary). The polygon $P$ is called rational if all of its interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$, and irrational otherwise. The billiard flow on $P$ is ergodic if every flow-invariant measurable subset of the phase space has either zero or full Liouville measure.

Question: Does there exist an irrational polygon $P$ whose billiard flow is not ergodic? Equivalently, exhibit a polygon at least one of whose interior angles is an irrational multiple of $\pi$, such that the associated billiard flow fails to be ergodic with respect to Liouville measure.
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on polygonal billiards (Masur–Tabachnikov; Schwartz's ICM survey; expository accounts) describe the question of whether there exists an irrational polygon whose billiard flow is nonergodic as a well-known open problem. Partial results exist (e.g., construction of nonergodic directions in certain polygons, and ergodicity for generic polygons), but no example of a fully nonergodic irrational polygon is known.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of an irrational polygon whose billiard flow fails to be ergodic is listed among open problems in polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of constructing a nonergodic irrational polygon is stated as open.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of billiards in non-rational polygons
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of attempts to use Liouville-type irrational polygons approximated by rational ones to transfer nonergodic behavior; the existence of a nonergodic irrational polygon remains unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The question is still open, though partial constructions of nonergodic directions exist.

status_evidence.title: Survey lecture on billiards (Schwartz, ICM)
status_evidence.snippet: Ergodicity of billiards in irrational polygons remains a wide-open question.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity vs. nonergodicity for irrational polygons is open.
